title: A Cellar for the Winter
premise: Hazel Dravenmoor, a property surveyor with a habit of documenting everything as a shield against her own past, is sent to appraise Dravenmoor House, the derelict family estate she fled at nine years old. Waiting on the porch is Wren, the imaginary friend she invented during a terrible winter, unchanged by thirty years and no longer content to be imagined. As Hazel surveys room after room, she realizes the house has been keeping its own ledger of debts, that her family's fortune was built on a bargain sealed in song, and that the well on the grounds refills every generation with what was promised. To survive the winter solstice, Hazel must learn the song's final verse from the house's previous victims without singing along herself, choose between loyalty to the found family she builds among the trapped and the truth that frees them, and decide whether power over the house is worth becoming the thing that holds it. She ends the bargain by singing the verse alone into the emptied well, freeing the trapped souls including Wren, who chooses to finally fade, while Hazel walks away owning nothing but her own documented truth.
about_author: Wendell Hartwell is the pen name of a former land registry clerk from coastal Maine who spent eleven years cataloguing deeds to houses that burned, flooded, or simply stopped appearing on maps. Their fiction explores the paperwork of haunting: what we sign, what we inherit, and what refuses to be filed away.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Her firm assigns her the Dravenmoor appraisal; she recognizes the address and almost refuses, then accepts, telling herself it's just a job. She packs her instruments and her notebooks. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Porch Light
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She arrives at dusk and finds Wren sitting on the porch steps, exactly as he looked when she was nine, waiting as if she'd only been gone an afternoon. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: Inventory of Rooms
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She begins the survey methodically, photographing and measuring, but rooms appear larger inside than out, and one hallway isn't on any floor plan. Emotional beat: the comfort of documentation fraying.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He explains he never left; the house kept him when Hazel stopped needing him. He's gentle, patient, and hungry for her attention. Emotional beat: tenderness with something wrong underneath.

chapters.title: The Well
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She finds the well behind the collapsed greenhouse, dry, ringed with carved names including her own in a child's handwriting. Emotional beat: recognition she can't yet name.

chapters.title: Neighbors Who Don't Visit
chapters.summary: Tomas, a retired mail carrier from the village, warns Hazel off over coffee at his kitchen table. His sister went up to the house in 1987. Emotional beat: first hint of a pattern, and of an ally.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the study she finds her grandfather's ledger: payments recorded not in money but in verses, dates, and names. The last entry is blank except for 'H.' Emotional beat: horror arriving through bookkeeping.

chapters.title: First Verse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At nightfall Wren hums a tune by the hearth, and the walls seem to lean in. Hazel catches herself humming back and stops, frightened by how natural it feels. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging.

chapters.title: The Winter Residents
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She discovers cold spots that move like people: a woman in the nursery, a man on the stairs, a child under the eaves. They are the previous singers. Emotional beat: grief for strangers.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (one of the trapped). Maren, trapped since 1961, reaches hazily toward Hazel, trying to speak through frost on windows. Emotional beat: desperate hope.

chapters.title: Appraisal Back
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Her measurements now return impossible figures; the house is valuing her, itemizing her fears in the margins of her own reports. Emotional beat: loss of the observer's safety.

chapters.title: Loyalty of Small Things
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas drives up uninvited with supplies and stays the night in his truck, refusing to leave her alone. Emotional beat: found family beginning, stubbornly.

chapters.title: Second Verse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren teaches Hazel the second verse openly, claiming it will protect her. The temperature drops; the residents gather to listen. Emotional beat: trust offered by an unreliable friend.

chapters.title: The Bargain's Shape
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Cross-referencing ledger and parish records, she reconstructs the deal: her ancestors traded the town's children, one per generation, for the house's endurance. Emotional beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Nursery Frost
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren manages one clear message scratched in frost: DON'T LEARN THE LAST. Then she's gone silent for days. Emotional beat: warning versus desperation.

chapters.title: The Firm Calls
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Her employer pressures her to finish; her report drafts keep rewriting themselves overnight into glowing praise of the property. Emotional beat: institutional indifference as complicity.

chapters.title: Under the Eaves
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She finds the child resident, Edda, age seven, trapped since 1934, who remembers Hazel's grandmother kindly. Emotional beat: the monstrous revealed as wounded.

chapters.title: Wren's Jealousy
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren grows cold when Hazel spends time with the residents instead of him; doors lock themselves between them. Emotional beat: love curdling into possession.

chapters.title: Third Verse
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The house itself sings the third verse through the pipes, and Hazel transcribes it rather than repeating it, learning to receive without giving voice. Emotional beat: discipline as resistance.

chapters.title: Tomas's Sister
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Searching his sister's belongings, Tomas finds her survey notes from 1987, ending mid-sentence. He brings them to Hazel. Emotional beat: grief converted to purpose.

chapters.title: The Refilling
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On the first frost, the well makes a sound like swallowing. Water rises in it, black and still, and the residents all turn toward it at once. Emotional beat: countdown begun.

chapters.title: What Power Costs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses he could take the house's power if Hazel would sing the last verse with him, making them both permanent, together forever. Emotional beat: temptation framed as devotion.

chapters.title: Edda's Song
chapters.summary: Edda's POV. Edda teaches Hazel a lullaby fragment, the fourth verse, sung by children before they were taken. It's the key to hearing the last verse safely. Emotional beat: innocence as inheritance.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The house seals itself for winter; roads vanish under snow, phone lines die, Tomas's truck won't start. They are residents now. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and resolve.

chapters.title: The Fifth Resident
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She counts the cold spots and finds six. The sixth is new, formed recently, wearing her grandmother's posture. Emotional beat: the cycle already claiming again.

chapters.title: Ledger Reconciliation
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She audits the ledger fully and finds the flaw: every bargain required a willing singer. No one ever had to sing alone. Emotional beat: hope hidden in fine print.

chapters.title: Wren's Origin
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits he was the first taken, a neighbor boy from 1902, reshaped by Hazel's childhood need into something comforting. Emotional beat: pity warring with fear.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hearth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Desperate, Wren tries to force the song, holding Hazel's voice in the air around her throat. Tomas breaks a window; the house flinches. Emotional beat: loyalty tested to breaking.

chapters.title: Exile Within
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The house punishes Wren, walling him into the cellar, and offers Hazel his place at its side. She declines. Emotional beat: refusal of corrupted power.

chapters.title: Maren's Memory
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Restored briefly by Hazel's attention, Maren recalls the last verse's melody but not its words, and warns that the words come from the well itself. Emotional beat: fragments as treasure.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel opens the cellar and goes down to Wren, notebook in hand, choosing to face him rather than let the house use their rupture. Emotional beat: courage as accountability.

chapters.title: The Cellar Conversation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the dark, Wren and Hazel speak honestly for the first time: about being left, about being made, about what they owe each other. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The residents gather; the well brims; the house hums the first five verses through every wall. Tomorrow it expects completion. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Last Verse Heard
chapters.summary: Edda's POV. At midnight the well sings the final verse in many small voices. Edda carries it to Hazel note by note, unsung aloud. Emotional beat: transmission of dangerous knowledge through trust.

chapters.title: Choosing Not to Sing Along
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Wren begs her once more to sing it with him; the house offers her everything. She writes the verse down instead, and the pages burn. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the record she trusts most.

chapters.title: Into the Well
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At dawn Hazel stands at the well and sings the last verse alone, voice steady, taking the debt onto herself alone so no one else ever has to. Emotional beat: climax; terror transfigured into agency.

chapters.title: The Emptying
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The well drains; the house exhales; Maren, Edda, and the others dissolve into light and cold clean air. The walls settle into ordinary decay. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Freed, Wren could persist as memory or fade entirely. He chooses to go, thanking Hazel for imagining him, and for letting him stop. Emotional beat: love meaning goodbye.

chapters.title: Final Appraisal
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel files a true report: structure unsound, property condemned, demolition recommended. The firm accepts it without question. Emotional beat: quiet victory of honest work.

chapters.title: Spring Survey
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Months later, Hazel and Tomas visit the razed lot where the capped well sits under wildflowers. She closes her notebook, no longer needing it as prayer. Emotional beat: peace earned, grief carried lightly.
